study.research_problem: Titanium particles are found in peri-implant tissues and may influence immune responses, but the immune-cell composition and cytokine signals associated with particles, peri-implantitis, and implant failure are not well resolved.
study.exact_gap: The study combines human gingival-tissue transcriptomics from failed, early successful, and no-implant sites with histology/IHC and a macrophage TiO2 exposure experiment; it seeks mechanistic plausibility, not direct bone-interface or longitudinal osseointegration evidence (S002:C04-S002:C05).
study.objective_or_hypothesis: Compare gene expression and inferred immune composition across failed, successful, and no-implant gingival tissues, identify titanium-like particles and immune cells histologically, and test whether commercial TiO2 micro/nanoparticles stimulate selected cytokines in THP-1-derived macrophages (S002:C05).
study.study_design: Cross-sectional three-group clinical tissue study (11 failed, 6 early successful, 3 no-implant patients) using AmpliSeq RNA profiling, DEG/enrichment/network/deconvolution analyses and CD3/CD68 histology, followed by 24-hour THP-1 M0 macrophage exposure to 20 or 100 micrograms per millilitre of commercial TiO2 nanoparticles/microparticles (S013:C01-S028:C01).
study.sample_or_model: Twenty selected adults: failed peri-implantitis explantation tissue 1-5 years after loading, successful-implant uncovering tissue roughly 3-6 months after placement, and peri-coronal tissue from impacted wisdom teeth; plus THP-1-derived macrophages and commercial TiO2 particles (S014:C01-S015:C02; S024:C01-S026:C01).
comparators: Failed implant gingiva versus no-implant gingiva
Early successful implant gingiva versus no-implant gingiva
Limited direct failed versus successful IHC comparison
Untreated THP-1 macrophages versus 20 and 100 micrograms per millilitre TiO2 nanoparticles or microparticles
No patient-level particle-burden gradient, longitudinal success/failure, microbial, bone-interface, or clinical intervention comparator
method_spine: Define clinical groups and harvest timing/site before interpreting molecular differences.
Profile bulk tissue and distinguish DEGs, pathways, and computational cell fractions.
Use histology/IHC to localize broad immune-cell classes and visually identify particle-like material.
Use a simplified particle-exposure cell model for selected cytokine plausibility.
Separate association, computational inference, morphology-based particle identification, and causal particle exposure.
Stop before osteoclast/bone-resorption/osseointegration claims that were not directly tested.

verification: RNA quality/read thresholds, DESeq2 FDR filtering, pathway tools, positive tonsil IHC controls, two pathologists, THP-1 differentiation check, and TiO2 DLS/SEM support technical execution (S017:C01-S028:C01).
Particle identity in human H&E was based on black-spot morphology without elemental confirmation, size quantification, or patient-level burden measurement (S008:C01; S012:C04-S012:C06).
calibration: No clinical particle-dose calibration links commercial TiO2 exposures to particle composition, size, concentration, or surface chemistry in patient tissue (S012:C06; S025:C01).
validation: CD68/CD3 IHC confirms broad macrophage/lymphocyte infiltration, while THP-1 cytokine responses support particle-inflammatory plausibility; neither validates CIBERSORT M1/M2 fractions, patient-specific causation, osteoclast activation, bone loss, or osseointegration failure (S009:C01-S010:C01).
The commercial TiO2 cell experiment is not a validation of particles visually observed in human tissue because composition, dose, morphology, and chronic exposure are unmatched.
sensitivity: Two particle sizes and two nominal concentrations reveal dose/size response for selected cytokines; no time-course, agglomeration/delivered dose, endotoxin, viability, surface chemistry, patient covariate, microbial, or tissue-composition sensitivity is reported.

The human groups differ structurally in time since implantation, disease, anatomy, sampling indication, and exposure history, preventing a clean sensitivity attribution to particle presence (S012:C09-S015:C02).
application_prediction: Early particle detection, diagnostic biomarkers, and immune-targeted therapies are future hypotheses; diagnostic accuracy, prospective failure prediction, and treatment response were not studied (S012:C10; S029:C01).

primary_outcomes: Bulk RNA profiles differed between failed/no-implant and successful/no-implant tissues, with 2185 and 5375 DEGs and enrichment of several immune/stress pathways (S003:C01-S005:C01).

CIBERSORT estimated differing M1/M2 and T-cell fractions, including M2 22.3% in failed versus 18.7% in successful tissues and M1 9.4% versus 9.9%, but these were computational estimates from small bulk-tissue groups (S006:C01).

H&E showed visually identified particle-like black material in both failed and successful implant tissue and more chronic inflammatory-cell infiltration in failed samples; CD68 and CD3 IHC were higher in failed than successful tissue (S008:C01-S009:C01).

At 100 micrograms per millilitre, commercial TiO2 nano- and microparticles increased IL-1beta, IL-8, and IL-18 secretion from THP-1-derived macrophages; TNF-alpha was not significantly changed, and several dose contrasts were significant (S010:C01).
STRING/PPI connected selected cytokines with known network neighbors, providing hypothesis organization rather than experimental interaction validation (S011:C01).
study.highest_evidence_level_reached: Small cross-sectional human soft-tissue molecular association plus simplified in-vitro macrophage exposure; no quantified human titanium burden, direct bone-interface biology, longitudinal failure prediction, or causal osseointegration evidence.

argument_map.central_claim: Failed peri-implant tissues contain greater broad immune-cell infiltration than early successful/no-implant tissues, and high-dose commercial TiO2 can stimulate selected macrophage cytokines in vitro, supporting a particle-associated inflammatory hypothesis; the data do not show that patient titanium particles caused the molecular differences, macrophage polarization, bone resorption, or implant failure.
data: Small-group bulk transcriptomic/enrichment/deconvolution results, morphology-based H&E particle observations, CD3/CD68 IHC, and TiO2-exposed THP-1 cytokines (S003:C01-S011:C01).
Clinical group definitions expose large differences in tissue site, disease state, and time since placement/loading (S014:C01-S015:C02).
argument_map.warrant: Convergence of clinical-tissue immune association and a controlled particle-exposure response supports biological plausibility, but causal attribution requires confirmed particle identity/burden, temporally comparable groups, microbial/confounder control, patient-particle matching, and direct bone outcomes.
backing: Particles appear in both successful and failed tissues, and the authors acknowledge microbial factors, small samples, unavailable patient macrophages, and unrecognized particle size (S012:C04-S012:C10).
argument_map.qualifier: Hypothesis-generating association in selected gingival tissues with short in-vitro particle exposure.
rebuttals_or_boundaries: Successful samples are early uncovering tissue at about 3-6 months, failed samples are diseased tissue 1-5 years after loading, and no-implant samples come from wisdom-tooth sites; group differences are not exposure-matched (S012:C09; S015:C01-S015:C02).
Titanium identity and quantity in patient tissue were not confirmed by SEM-EDS/ICP or correlated with cytokines/outcome; black H&E spots are not element-specific (S008:C01; S012:C04-S012:C06).
Peri-implantitis infection/biofilm, reverse causality, crown micro-gap, corrosion, intervention, and inflammation-driven wear remain alternative explanations (S012:C05-S012:C09).
CD68 is pan-macrophage and CD3 is broad T-cell staining; neither directly validates M1/M2 polarization, and proposed CD86/CD163 work was future (S012:C02).
Commercial TiO2 doses/particles may not match patient wear debris, and no osteoblast, osteoclast, bone resorption, BIC, fixation, or implant survival was measured.

measured: Clinical group/tissue data, targeted RNA counts, CD3/CD68 staining, morphology-based H&E observations, commercial particle characterization, and THP-1 cytokine concentrations (S003:C01-S010:C01; S013:C01-S028:C01).
predicted: CIBERSORT cell fractions, enriched pathways, leading-edge genes, and STRING interaction networks are computational inferences from bulk expression/reference databases rather than directly counted cell subtypes or measured protein interactions (S004:C01-S006:C01; S011:C01).
inferred: Distinct group transcriptomes are attributed to titanium-particle impact despite unmeasured particle burden and major group/time/site confounding (S012:C01).
Common immune pathways in both implant groups are treated as evidence of particle-triggered immunity, although implantation/surgery/tissue location and other exposures also differ (S012:C03).
CD68/CD3 infiltration plus TiO2 cytokines is extended to macrophage polarization, osteoclast activation, bone resorption, and failed osseointegration without direct measurement (S012:C05-S012:C10).
Bioinformatics tools are described as overcoming small sample size; they can organize signals but do not restore power or eliminate selection/confounding bias (S012:C10).
recommended: Confirm human particle identity, composition, size, and tissue burden; use time/site-matched longitudinal groups, microbiome/confounder measures, direct M1/M2 markers and spatial methods, patient-derived cells/particles, delivered-dose controls, and bone-interface outcomes.
proxy_to_outcome_bridges: Bulk RNA pathway enrichment is not direct immune-cell function or causal pathway activation.
CIBERSORT percentages are model-derived cell-composition estimates, not histological counts.
CD68/CD3 and cytokines do not establish osteoclast activity or bone resorption.
Gingival soft-tissue inflammation is not direct bone-implant osseointegration failure.
Commercial TiO2 macrophage exposure is not patient wear-particle causality.
Particle presence in successful and failed tissue means presence alone is not a failure discriminator.
overclaim_risks: The title and conclusion say titanium particles modulate lymphocyte/macrophage polarization, but clinical exposure is cross-sectional/unquantified and direct polarization markers are absent (S001:C01; S029:C01).
The paper repeatedly connects cytokines to osteoblast-osteoclast imbalance and failure of osseointegration without bone-interface measurements (S011:C01-S012:C10).
H&E black spots are called titanium particles based on morphology rather than element-specific analysis (S008:C01).
A STRING network is presented as functional interconnection, not experimental molecular interaction or causal validation (S011:C01).
The finite-element and in-vivo-animal cues are false; this study is clinical cross-sectional plus in-vitro.

section_moves.move: Map every evidence modality to the question it can answer
section_moves.execution: Bulk RNA identifies associations, deconvolution predicts cell fractions, IHC localizes broad cell classes, and THP-1 exposure tests selected cytokine plausibility (S017:C01-S026:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: For multimodal mechanobiology, state the inferential role of each modality and prohibit one assay from validating a different latent construct.
section_moves.failure_mode: IHC for CD68/CD3 does not validate M1/M2 deconvolution or bone-resorption mechanisms.

section_moves.execution: Particle-like material and immune pathways occur in both successful and failed implant tissues, while infiltration is greater in failures (S007:C01-S009:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: When an exposure appears in both outcome groups, write burden, timing, context, and moderator hypotheses rather than treating presence as sufficient causation.
section_moves.failure_mode: Particle presence alone cannot classify failure.

section_moves.move: Expose temporal and anatomical comparator mismatch
section_moves.execution: The discussion explains why successful tissue came from early uncovering, failed tissue from later explantation, and no-implant tissue from wisdom-tooth sites (S012:C09; S015:C01-S015:C02).
section_moves.transferable_principle: In clinical tissue omics, report site, disease state, procedure, time since implantation/loading, and sampling indication as comparator-defining variables, not background details.
section_moves.failure_mode: Cross-sectional group omics cannot isolate an implant-particle effect when tissue histories differ.

section_moves.move: Build a mechanism ladder and stop at the missing bone link
section_moves.execution: The paper connects particles to macrophage cytokines and literature osteoclast pathways, but lacks direct osteoclast/bone outcomes (S012:C06-S012:C10).
section_moves.transferable_principle: Write exposure-to-failure chains link by link—particle burden, cell uptake, cytokine, polarization, osteoclast, resorption, fixation—and label each measured, predicted, inferred, or missing.
section_moves.failure_mode: Do not collapse cytokine plausibility into demonstrated osseointegration failure.

author_reported: The authors acknowledge small clinical groups, use of THP-1 rather than patient macrophages, inability to recognize particle size in tissue, and the need to assess titanium content and microbial factors (S012:C05-S012:C10).
reader_identified: Severe group mismatch in sampling time, anatomical site, disease status, surgical indication, and exposure history.
Human particle identity/burden is morphology-based and unquantified; no within-patient particle-inflammation/outcome association.
No direct FI-versus-SI transcriptomic model is emphasized, and very small n with many genes/pathways risks unstable estimates; GSEA uses nominal p-value language.
CIBERSORT appears applied to DEG lists and reports precise fractions without uncertainty; M1/M2 is not directly stained with subtype markers.
Commercial TiO2 exposure lacks patient-particle matching, delivered-dose/agglomeration/endotoxin/viability/time-course controls.
No microbial, osteoclast, osteoblast, bone-resorption, BIC, micro-motion, or longitudinal implant outcome measurement.
Network database analysis is hypothesis generation, not interaction validation.
likely_bias_direction: Late diseased failure tissue versus early successful tissue likely exaggerates failure-associated immune differences.
Morphological particle assignment and unmeasured microbial confounding favor a titanium-causal narrative.
Multiple bioinformatics layers may make a small, confounded sample appear more validated than it is.
limitations.scope_boundary: The study supports an association between failed peri-implant gingival tissue and greater immune infiltration plus the capacity of commercial TiO2 to stimulate selected macrophage cytokines. It does not establish patient titanium-particle causality, M1/M2 polarization, bone resorption, or failed osseointegration.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Write multimodal clinical mechanobiology as separate measured, computationally predicted, and inferred layers, with each validation modality tied to its actual target.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Methods evidence map, Results ordering, Discussion, and claim audit.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: CIBERSORT, CD68/CD3, and THP-1 cytokines answer different questions and do not jointly prove polarization or bone failure.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Audit clinical tissue comparators by anatomical site, disease state, sampling indication, time since implantation/loading, and exposure history before causal interpretation.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Cohort table, comparator-fairness paragraph, and limitations.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: Early uncovering tissue, late peri-implantitis explant tissue, and wisdom-tooth gingiva are not exchangeable controls.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Trace particle-to-failure claims as an explicit causal ladder and require exposure identity/burden, cellular response, bone-resorption, and fixation links before writing osseointegration failure.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Mechanism figure, Discussion, and translational conclusion.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: Soft-tissue cytokines after commercial TiO2 exposure do not demonstrate patient-particle-driven osteoclast resorption or implant loosening.

critical_weaknesses: Small, temporally and anatomically mismatched clinical groups.
Human titanium exposure and macrophage polarization are not directly quantified/validated.
No bone-interface or longitudinal evidence bridges inflammation to osseointegration failure.

summary_zh: 这项研究把 11 例失败植体、6 例早期成功植体和 3 例无植体牙龈组织的 bulk RNA、计算去卷积、H&E/IHC 与 THP-1 颗粒暴露串联起来。可重复的信号是失败组 CD68/CD3 浸润更高，商业 TiO2 在高剂量下可提高部分巨噬细胞细胞因子；但因果链远未闭合。成功组是植入后约 3–6 个月的二期暴露组织，失败组是负载 1–5 年后的炎症组织，无植体组又来自智齿区，比较器在时间、部位和疾病状态上严重不匹配。人体所谓钛颗粒仅按 H&E 黑点形态判断，没有元素确认或负荷定量；CD68/CD3 也不验证 M1/M2。最重要的 Skill 规则是逐段标注：bulk RNA/细胞因子为 measured，CIBERSORT/PPI 为 predicted，颗粒导致极化—破骨—骨丧失—骨整合失败则是 inferred/missing。
reader_notes: Primary Codex reader reviewed every non-reference packet section, including all ten Discussion chunks and the complete clinical/in-vitro methods.
The finite-element and in-vivo-animal cues are false.
The paper's strongest evidence is failure-associated broad immune infiltration plus TiO2 cytokine plausibility, not titanium-particle causation or direct osseointegration failure.
